doc.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: Getting into the San Diego scene and Holly Hofmann
summary: Using school to enter the community, the Horton Grand Hotel, Holly Hofmann as mentor, and other San Diego players.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So after you got your education up to the point where you felt pretty confident, did you have to choose between the East Coast and the West Coast? Or did it just kind of happen for you that you ended up—

Well by the time I had my master’s I was already working. My goal was while I was in school I was trying to get out of school as fast as possible, musically speaking. So while I was doing my studies, because I was watching the people around me that weren’t necessarily there — they weren’t jazzers, it’s not a jazz school. But I would see them with the avant garde thing. And they would be so intent on the performances for those school concerts and those ensembles at school that they never saw the community. They never integrated themselves. And then they would end up staying for their Ph.D.s because they didn’t have anywhere else to go. And for me I wanted to use the schooling to get my chops together. And to me, taking those lessons and doing the studies that I had to do to get the degree was to get me out into the community. So the first weekend I was in town I went down to the Horton Grand Hotel, which is where the jazz stuff was happening in San Diego. So I’d go down there every weekend and hang out with the musicians and learn and listen. They used to call me “the kid.” It’s the kid again. So I met Holly Hofmann, who was a wonderful mentor for me there. She has been really supportive and encouraging and real honest with me when I’ve been playing well and when I haven’t been playing well. That was a wonderful opportunity. So like by the time I got done with the degree I’ve just been in San Diego.
There’s a few other good fellas there and players in San Diego.

Oh yeah, James Moody, Charles McPherson, Mundell Lowe, Barney Kessel lives there, although you know of course with the stroke he’s not playing. But yeah, every once in a while he’ll come to one of my gigs and hang out. It’s marvelous. It’s really cool.
